references.text: The entire chapter 13 in Leviticus describes the laws concerning leprosy and how the priest is to examine and diagnose the disease, which forms the background for the cleansing ritual in chapter 14.
Summary law regarding the leper who cannot afford the usual offerings at his cleansing.
Concerns that lepers must be sent outside the camp and may return when they are clean.
Reminder to follow the priests' guidance concerning leprosy.
The account of Naaman, who was healed of leprosy and sent to the priest to show himself as clean.
Jesus heals a leper and commands him to show himself to the priest and offer the sacrifice that Moses commanded, referring to Leviticus 14.
Jesus heals a leper and sends him to the priest to offer what Moses prescribed as a testimony to them.
Jesus heals a leprous man and commands him to go to the priest and offer for his cleansing as Moses commanded.
Jesus heals ten lepers and sends them to the priests to be declared clean.
